question: When fuel evaporates and spreads into the atmosphere, what is this emission called?
solution:
The correct answer is __Evaporative emissions**(Option 4)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Evaporative emissions__ occur when fuel evaporates and spreads into the atmosphere.
 
• These emissions typically result from fuel systems in vehicles.
 
• They are a significant source of air pollution and contribute to smog formation.
 
• The primary cause of evaporative emissions is volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in fuels.
 
• These emissions can occur even when vehicles are not in use.
 
• Modern vehicles are equipped with evaporative emission control systems (EVAP) to reduce these emissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Combustion Emissions:**

 
 
• These are emissions released during the burning of fuel in an engine.
 
• They primarily include carbon dioxide (CO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ).
 
 
 
• **Crankcase Emissions:**
 
 
• These emissions originate from the engine crankcase, due to combustion gas leakage.
 
• Modern vehicles use positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) systems to mitigate these emissions.
 
 
 
• **Exhaust Emissions:**
 
 
• These are emissions released through the vehicle's exhaust system.
 
• They include pollutants like hydrocarbons (HC), carbon monoxide (CO), and particulate matter.
